terms.gloss: the one who hires workers: an employer
evidence: Plaut. Asin. 3: gregīque huic et dominīs atque conductōribus, the troupe, its owners and those who hire it
terms.comment: The party who condūcit, hires, labour as well as a house (see tenant); a woman is conductrīx (Traupman 309). To hire labourers, operāriōs condūcere (Cato Agr. 4).

evidence: Levi–Bini p. 51: principale, the head of a firm
terms.comment: Classically the master of a household and its slaves, and the owner of a business (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Ille quī mē condūxit, ubi condūxit, abdūxit domum, quae voluit mihi dīxit, docuit et praemōnstrāvit prius, quō modō quicque agerem
phrases.english: The man who hired me took me home the moment he had hired me; he told me what he wanted, and taught me and showed me beforehand how to do each thing

phrases.latin: Sī tē libenter vīcīnitās vidēbit, facilius tua vēndēs, opera facilius locābis, operāriōs facilius condūcēs
phrases.english: If the neighbours like to see you, you will sell your produce more easily, let out your work more easily and hire labourers more easily

sources: Lewis & Short: conductor · Lewis & Short: dominus
